title: Hanoverian Succession (George I, 1714)
key_facts: Succession of George I of Hanover to the British throne under the Act of Settlement (1701)
Marked the start of the Hanoverian dynasty in Britain
Accelerated the development of cabinet government and party politics
causes: Protestant succession mandated by the Act of Settlement (1701)
Deaths of preceding heirs and Queen Anne without surviving issue
Desire to avoid a Catholic Stuart restoration
outcome: George I crowned; Whig ascendency consolidated
Growth of ministerial government and fiscal‑military state
Closer linkage between British and Hanoverian interests

figures.name: George I
figures.role: First Hanoverian king of Great Britain

figures.name: Robert Walpole
figures.role: Leading Whig statesman; often considered first de facto prime minister

impacts: Stabilized Protestant succession and constitutional monarchy
Catalyzed cabinet governance and party system
Shaped 18th‑century British domestic and foreign policy
